page: Microsoft Azure D64s_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processors operating at clock speeds up to 4.2 GHz. The compute configuration delivers 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with 2 threads per core using an x86_64 architecture. Hardware acceleration features include Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX tile and int8) and AVX-512 extensions (including VNNI and BF16). The CPU architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 260 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 256.0 GB, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance has no integrated GPUs and provides no local ephemeral storage, relying on external Premium Storage for persistence.

Benchmark measurements indicate competitive parallel compute capability and memory throughput. The server achieved a top-tier Geekbench multi-core score of 21,795.0 alongside a single-core score of 2,147.0. Large-block memory tests registered 259.69 GB/sec read bandwidth and 110.72 GB/sec write bandwidth, complemented by strong results in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (391.6 GB/sec) and gzip compression (31.53 GB/sec). High-concurrency operations show solid performance, with static web serving throughput reaching 97.36 GB/sec and Redis SET operations measuring 82.05 million operations per second. Hardware matrix instructions also facilitate CPU-based LLM inference, reaching 3,294.26 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 135M model and 38.39 tokens per second for text generation on a 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D64s_v6 delivers dense vCPU and memory allocation tailored for workloads that require heavy multi-threading without the overhead of GPU silicon. A notable architectural tradeoff is the absence of local scratch disks, requiring networked block storage to be provisioned separately. This server fits enterprise-scale web servers, large multi-threaded application runtimes, in-memory caching platforms, and data pre-processing pipelines.

Built on x86_64 architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, it features dedicated core allocation, AVX-512, and AMX instructions alongside a 260 MB L3 cache. System memory totals 256.0 GB, adhering to a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The server includes no GPUs and lacks local storage, requiring remote Premium Storage disks. Performance benchmarks reveal strong multi-threaded execution, high static web serving throughput of 97.36 GB/sec, and 82.05 million Redis SET operations per second. With AMX-accelerated CPU inference capabilities, the D64s_v6 is positioned for dense multi-threaded microservices, large caching layers, compile farms, and relational database servers.
